newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao leaves court after hearing adjourned.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao leaves court after hearing adjourned.

text.p: Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao left a trial court on Wednesday after the judge adjourned the bail hearing for lunch, witnesses said.
Rao, surrounded by Congress party leaders who attended the morning hearing, left the annexe of New Delhi's Vigyan Bhavan conference complex in a convoy of cars.
Rao's lawyer R.K. Anand told Reuters his client had been exempted from attending the afternoon session and Rao would not return to the court room once the hearing resumed.
Before the luncheon adjournment, chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar said the hearing would continue on Thursday, indicating that no ruling on Rao's request for bail would come before then.
Anand said Rao would attend Thursday's hearing.
During the three and a half hour morning session, Anand argued that temporary bail which was granted to Rao earlier this month and expires on November 6 should be extended.
The counsel for the Central Bureau of Investigation, C. Sahay, argued that the judge was entitled to remand Rao and the five other co-accused to judicial custody.
